proofs.text: In a git checkout at the gate `passed`, run `--all --record --commit`; verify `Record committed as developer.`, that the record's `commit` differs from HEAD because the record's own commit came after it, and that the rule's passed cell reads `passed`. Change the scoped file `src/feat.py` and commit it; verify the passed cell reads `code changed`

rule_text: A record carries the git tree hash of its feature's scoped files, so a rule's passed cell reads `passed` while only other files change and reads `code changed` once a scoped file changes

tests.body:
def test_a_committed_record_makes_the_passed_cell_read_passed(
            self, tmp_path):
        root = _pytest_project(tmp_path)
        (root / 'src').mkdir()
        (root / 'src' / 'feat.py').write_text('VALUE = 2\n', encoding='utf-8')
        _spec(root, 'feat')
        _git_repo(root)

        assert _rule(root, 'feat', 'RULE-1')['spec'] == 'drafted'

        code, out = _run(root, '--all', '--record', '--commit')
        assert code == 0, out
        assert 'Record committed as developer.' in out, out

        record = _newest_record(root, 'feat')
        assert isinstance(record['scope_tree'], str), record['scope_tree']
        assert record['proofs'][0]['id'] == 'PROOF-1'
        assert record['proofs'][0]['status'] == 'pass'
        assert record['feature'] == 'feat'
        assert record['gate'] == 'passed'

        # The record is one commit behind HEAD, which is the case the scope
        # tree exists to cover.
        assert record['commit'] != _head(root)
        assert _passed_word(root, 'feat', 'RULE-1') == 'passed'
tests.name: test_a_committed_record_makes_the_passed_cell_read_passed

def test_the_cell_reads_code_changed_when_the_scope_changed(self, tmp_path):
        root = _pytest_project(tmp_path)
        (root / 'src').mkdir()
        (root / 'src' / 'feat.py').write_text('VALUE = 2\n', encoding='utf-8')
        _spec(root, 'feat')
        _git_repo(root)
        code, out = _run(root, '--all', '--record', '--commit')
        assert code == 0, out
        assert _passed_word(root, 'feat', 'RULE-1') == 'passed'

        (root / 'src' / 'feat.py').write_text('VALUE = 3\n', encoding='utf-8')
        _git(root, 'add', '-A')
        _git(root, 'commit', '-q', '-m', 'change the scoped code')
        assert _passed_word(root, 'feat', 'RULE-1') == 'code changed'
tests.name: test_the_cell_reads_code_changed_when_the_scope_changed
